about: HCW Biologics is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing immunotherapies based on its TOBI discovery platform, which creates fusion proteins that activate natural killer cells and T cells, aimed at cancers and age-related inflammatory disease. Lead candidates include HCW9302 for alopecia areata and other autoimmune conditions. It is listed on Nasdaq (HCWB) and has no commercial products. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile and a small marketing budget.

HemoGenyx Pharmaceuticals is a small US biotechnology company, based in New York, developing a stem cell therapy approach for blood disorders and certain autoimmune diseases, aimed at replacing bone marrow transplants with a safer conditioning treatment. Its programmes remained preclinical or at an early clinical stage. It trades on the over-the-counter markets and has very limited resources. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

iBio is a US biotechnology company that has evolved from a plant-based contract development and manufacturing business into an AI-driven drug discovery and biologics developer, with programmes in obesity and cardiometabolic disease, oncology and antibody engineering. It sold its Texas CDMO facility and now concentrates on its discovery platform and pipeline, partly in cooperation with partners. Based in Newark, Delaware, with offices in San Diego, it is listed on NYSE American (IBIO). B2B biotech with no consumer profile.

J-Pharma is a Japanese biotechnology and pharmaceutical company based in Tokyo, tagged by Crunchbase under biotechnology and medical, and flagged here as listed. No description is available in the input. It appears to be a drug developer or specialty pharma business, but its products, pipeline, ownership and scale cannot be confirmed. Japanese specialty pharma firms usually sell through hospitals and wholesalers and have no consumer brand visibility. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Kiora Pharmaceuticals is a US clinical-stage ophthalmology company developing small-molecule drugs for retinal diseases, led by KIO-301, a photoswitch molecule intended to restore light sensitivity in blind retinal cells for retinitis pigmentosa, which is licensed in Asia to Senju Pharmaceutical. It has other earlier candidates for inflammatory eye conditions. Based in Encinitas, California, and listed on Nasdaq (KPRX), it has no approved product and relies on equity financing and partner payments. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Lucid Diagnostics is a US commercial-stage medical diagnostics company, a majority-owned subsidiary of PAVmed, selling the EsoCheck cell collection device and EsoGuard DNA test to screen for Barrett's esophagus and detect risk of esophageal cancer in people with chronic acid reflux. It sells through its own centres and to physicians, with payers gradually reimbursing the test. Based in New York and listed on Nasdaq (LUCD), it has small revenue and heavy losses. Consumer awareness is low, though it markets to patients with reflux.

MindMaze, formerly Relief Therapeutics, is a Geneva-based Swiss pharmaceutical group listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange. Relief developed and marketed specialty and rare disease products and pursued the inhaled aviptadil drug for lung disease. The change of name points to a combination with MindMaze, a neurotechnology business known for digital therapeutics for stroke and brain injury rehabilitation, also Swiss-based. Details of the combined business should be checked. B2B healthcare company with no consumer profile.

Moleculin Biotech is a US clinical-stage pharmaceutical company developing oncology drugs for hard-to-treat cancers, led by Annamycin, an anthracycline designed to avoid cardiotoxicity and drug resistance, in trials for relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia and soft tissue sarcoma lung metastases. It also has WP1066 for brain tumours and WP1122 for viral infections. Based in Houston and listed on Nasdaq (MBRX), it has no approved product and depends on equity. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

NeOnc Technologies is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company developing brain cancer therapies built around perillyl alcohol derivatives, led by NEO100 and NEO212, which are designed to cross the blood-brain barrier, targeting glioblastoma and other high-grade gliomas. Based in Calabasas, California, with strong ties to the University of Southern California research tradition, it listed on Nasdaq (NTHI) in 2025. It has no commercial products. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

NervGen Pharma is a Canadian clinical-stage biotechnology company, based in Vancouver, developing NVG-291, a peptide designed to enable repair of damaged nerve connections after spinal cord injury, tested in the CONNECT SCI trial in chronic and acute injury. It also looks at other neurological conditions. It has no approved product, is funded by equity and partner contributions, and is listed on the TSX (NGEN) and OTC markets. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

Nuwellis is a US medical device company that makes the Aquadex SmartFlow system, an ultrafiltration therapy that removes excess fluid from patients with fluid overload, such as those with heart failure, and the Vivian blood-purification system for kidney-related care. It sells to hospitals and critical care units, and has a pediatric version. Formerly CHF Solutions, it is based in Eden Prairie, Minnesota, and listed on Nasdaq (NUWE) with small revenue. B2B medical device company with no consumer brand profile.

Opus Genetics, formerly Ocuphire Pharma, is a US clinical-stage ophthalmology company developing gene therapies for inherited retinal diseases such as LCA5 and BEST1-related conditions, alongside phentolamine eye drops for reversal of mydriasis, presbyopia and dim-light vision disturbances. It licensed phentolamine to Viatris. Based in Farmington Hills, Michigan, with research operations in the Durham area, it is listed on Nasdaq (IRD). Revenue comes from licensing and grants. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Pelthos Therapeutics is a US commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company, formed in 2025 through a merger involving Channel Therapeutics and Ligand's LNHC unit. It markets Zelsuvmi (berdazimer gel), a topical treatment for molluscum contagiosum approved by the FDA, in the paediatric dermatology market. Based in North Brunswick, New Jersey, and listed on NYSE American (PTHS), it sells through specialty pharmacies and dermatology practices. Customers are dermatologists and parents. B2B pharma with little consumer brand awareness.

Profusa is a US biosensor company developing tissue-integrated sensors, notably the Lumee oxygen-sensing platform, a tiny injectable hydrogel sensor that reads oxygen levels through the skin, intended for monitoring peripheral artery disease and critical limb ischemia and for wider health tracking. Founded in 2009 and based in Emeryville, California, it listed on Nasdaq (PFSA) via a 2024 SPAC merger. Revenue is minimal, mainly from grants and early commercial work. B2B medical technology with no consumer brand profile.

Quantum Biopharma, formerly FSD Pharma, is a Canadian biotechnology company based in Toronto, with a lead programme Lucid-MS for multiple sclerosis, a neuroprotective compound aimed at stopping myelin damage, plus Celly Nutrition, a consumer sports nutrition and wellness brand, and legacy interests in cannabis cultivation. It trades on Nasdaq and the Canadian Securities Exchange (QNTM). Revenue is small. Mostly pharma development, with a small consumer arm, Celly, with limited awareness.

Tempest Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage oncology company developing small-molecule drugs for cancers, led by amezalpat (TPST-1120), a PPAR-alpha antagonist being trialled with atezolizumab and bevacizumab in first-line hepatocellular carcinoma, and TPST-1495 targeting the EP2/EP4 pathway. It has no commercial products and funds research by equity raises. Based in Brisbane, California, and listed on Nasdaq (TPST). B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

TenNor Therapeutics is a clinical-stage anti-infective company, founded in China with operations in the US, developing new antibiotics for drug-resistant bacterial infections, including rifasutenizol (TNP-2092) for Helicobacter pylori and a series of candidates against resistant staph infections. It combines research in Suzhou with a US presence in New Jersey. It has raised venture funding and has no approved products. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

Traws Pharma is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, formed in 2024 by the merger of Onconova Therapeutics with Trawsfynydd Therapeutics, developing oral antivirals against influenza, including bird flu, and COVID-19, along with oncology drug rigosertib. Based in Newtown, Pennsylvania, it is listed on Nasdaq (TRAW). It has no product revenue and is funded by equity raises. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Valerio Therapeutics, formerly Onxeo, is a French biotechnology company based in the Paris area (Villejuif) that develops DNA damage response cancer drugs, including its AsiDNA platform of decoy molecules that interfere with tumour DNA repair. Listed on Euronext Paris, it has no commercial products and depends on equity financing and partnerships. Customers would be oncology providers. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile and a very small team.

Vivakor is a US company listed on Nasdaq (VIVK), based in Dallas, that has pivoted from remediation technology to oil gathering, storage, transportation and processing. It runs crude oil logistics and storage in Texas and other states, and uses soil remediation technology to recover oil from contaminated soils. Customers are refiners, oil producers and industrial users. Revenue is in the tens of millions of dollars, and it acquired Silver Fuels Delhi. B2B energy services firm with no consumer profile.

VivoSim Labs, formerly Organovo Holdings, is a US biotechnology company that develops 3D bioprinted and lab-grown human tissue models used to test drug toxicity and efficacy for pharmaceutical customers, as an alternative to animal testing. After a pivot from therapeutic tissue development it sold its FXR program to Lilly and rebranded in 2025. Based in San Diego and listed on Nasdaq (VIVS). B2B research-tools supplier with no consumer profile.

VolitionRx is a US-and-Belgium diagnostics company developing Nu.Q, a blood-based epigenetics platform that detects circulating nucleosomes for cancer screening and monitoring, including lung and colorectal tests and a veterinary cancer test for dogs. It sells research and lab-developed products and aims at regulatory approval for clinical use. Run from Henderson, Nevada, with laboratories in Namur, Belgium, and listed on NYSE American (VNRX). Revenue is tiny. B2B diagnostics firm with no consumer brand.

AB Science is a French pharmaceutical company, based in Paris and listed on Euronext (AB), that develops protein kinase inhibitors, led by masitinib, in trials for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Alzheimer's disease, multiple sclerosis, mastocytosis and cancers, and approved for veterinary use in dogs under the Masivet and Kinavet brands. Founded in 2001 by Alain Moussy, who remains CEO and a major shareholder. Revenue is small and comes from licensing. Customers are physicians and veterinarians. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

Adial Pharmaceuticals is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in Glen Allen, Virginia, developing AD04, a genetically targeted ondansetron treatment for alcohol use disorder in patients with specific genotypes, and other addiction and substance-use treatments. It is listed on Nasdaq (ADIL), has no approved product, and has separated its Purnovate subsidiary. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand and a small budget.

AFYREN is a French industrial biotechnology company that produces bio-based carboxylic acids, such as acetic, propionic, butyric, valeric and caproic acids, from non-food biomass using fermentation. Customers are makers of flavours and fragrances, animal nutrition, cosmetics, lubricants and chemicals who want low-carbon alternatives to petrochemical acids. Its first plant, AFYREN NEOXY, is in Carling, Lorraine. Founded in 2012 and based in Clermont-Ferrand, it is listed on Euronext Growth (AFYR). B2B chemicals firm with no consumer brand.

Atossa Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, based in Seattle, developing (Z)-endoxifen, an oral selective estrogen receptor modulator, for breast cancer in several settings, including neoadjuvant treatment, metastatic disease and breast density reduction. It started as a breast-health device company before pivoting to drug development. Listed on Nasdaq (ATOS), it has no commercial product and a cash-based funding model with sizeable reserves. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Avacta Group is a UK life sciences company, based in Wetherby, West Yorkshire, that developed Affimer engineered proteins and the pre|CISION peptide-drug conjugate platform, which releases chemotherapy only inside tumours. Its lead candidate AVA6000, a doxorubicin conjugate, is in clinical trials for solid tumours. It previously ran a diagnostics business through its Avacta Life Sciences division and sold a stake in the Affimer therapeutic programme to partners. Customers and partners are pharmaceutical firms and research groups. Listed on London's AIM market (AVCT). B2B biotech with no consumer brand profile.

BioHarvest Sciences is a Canadian biotechnology company, headquartered in Vancouver with research in Israel, that has a patented botanical synthesis platform to grow plant cells in bioreactors and produce active compounds. Its main consumer product is VINIA, a grape-cell dietary supplement rich in resveratrol and other polyphenols, sold directly to consumers online and through retailers, with additional ranges planned. It is also exploring other nutraceutical and pharmaceutical uses of the platform. Listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange and Nasdaq. Small consumer health brand with growing online marketing spend.

BrainStorm Cell Therapeutics is a US and Israeli biotechnology company, developing NurOwn, an autologous mesenchymal stem cell therapy for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), and later for other neurodegenerative diseases such as progressive multiple sclerosis. A Phase 3 trial in ALS missed its primary endpoint, and the company has since sought regulatory advice for a follow-on trial. It has no product revenue and is funded by equity. Dual offices in New York and Petach Tikva, and listed on Nasdaq (BCLI). B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

CERo Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage immuno-oncology company developing engineered T cells with a chimeric engulfment receptor (CER) platform, which turns T cells into cells that engulf and destroy tumour cells. Its lead candidate CER-1236 is in an early trial for acute myeloid leukemia. Based in South San Francisco, it listed on Nasdaq (CERO) in 2024 after a SPAC merger with Phoenix Biotech Acquisition. It has no product revenue. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

Cingulate Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing CTx-1301, a once-daily dexmethylphenidate tablet for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), built on its Precision Timed Release technology to cover the whole day. It has submitted the drug to the US FDA, and would sell to paediatric and adult ADHD patients through physicians. Based in Kansas City and listed on Nasdaq (CING), it has no commercial revenue yet. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

Citius Oncology is a US late-stage oncology company that markets LYMPHIR (denileukin diftitox-cxdl), an immunotherapy for relapsed or refractory cutaneous T-cell lymphoma approved by the FDA in 2024, and is working on other cancer immunotherapy combinations. It is the oncology subsidiary of Citius Pharmaceuticals, listed on Nasdaq (CTOR) after a 2024 SPAC merger. Based in Cranford, New Jersey, it sells to cancer centres and oncologists, and revenue is at an early stage. B2B pharma with no consumer profile.

Decoy Therapeutics is a Houston, Texas, biotechnology company in the Crunchbase health and medical tags, flagged as listed. The entry has no description, and the exact pipeline, partners, ownership and listing details cannot be confirmed from the available data. Companies using this name have been associated with antiviral peptide conjugates, but that cannot be verified here. Early-stage biotech firms of this kind have no consumer brand profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Enveric Biosciences is a US biotechnology company developing neuroplastogen drugs, derived from psychedelic-inspired molecules, for anxiety, depression and addiction, such as EVM201 and EB-003, and a library of novel compounds produced through its Psybrary programme. It licenses compounds to partners and has no commercial products. The company is based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, with roots in Naples, Florida, and listed on Nasdaq (ENVB). B2B drug developer with no consumer brand and small resources.

Ernexa Therapeutics, formerly Eterna Therapeutics and before that Brooklyn ImmunoTherapeutics, is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company developing allogeneic cell therapies from induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) for cancer and autoimmune disease, using a platform that produces engineered immune cells. Its lead programme ERNA-101 targets ovarian cancer. It has no commercial products and depends on equity funding. Based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and listed on Nasdaq (ERNA). B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

GT Biopharma is a US clinical-stage immuno-oncology company developing TriKE natural killer cell engager antibodies, notably GTB-3650 for CD33-positive blood cancers such as acute myeloid leukemia and myelodysplastic syndrome, and a candidate for solid tumours. The platform originates from University of Minnesota research. Based in Westlake Village, California, and listed on Nasdaq (GTBP), it has no commercial products and funds itself through equity raises. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Imricor Medical Systems is a US medical device company, based in Burnsville, Minnesota, developing the Vision-MR ablation catheter and related devices that let cardiologists treat heart arrhythmias such as atrial flutter using MRI guidance rather than X-ray, with no radiation exposure. It sells to hospitals in Europe and has US regulatory approvals in progress or recently cleared. Revenue is small. Listed on the Australian Securities Exchange (IMR). B2B medical device company with no consumer brand profile.

Imugene is an Australian clinical-stage immuno-oncology company, based in Sydney, developing azer-cel, an off-the-shelf allogeneic CD19-targeted CAR T-cell therapy for blood cancers, along with onCARlytics, an oncolytic virus platform, and vaccine candidates built on B-cell peptide technology. It has no approved products and runs trials in Australia and the US. Listed on the Australian Securities Exchange (IMU), it is funded by equity raises. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Indaptus Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company developing Decoy20, an intravenous immunotherapy made from killed, non-pathogenic bacteria that activates innate and adaptive immune cells against cancers and viral infections. It is investigated in combination with checkpoint inhibitors for solid tumours. Based in New York, with research links to Israel, it listed on Nasdaq (INDP) after a 2021 merger with Intec Pharma. No product revenue. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand.

Kairos Pharma is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company, based in Los Angeles, developing cancer therapeutics designed to counter drug resistance and immune suppression, led by ENV105, an antibody against CD105 (endoglin), tested with standard therapy in prostate and lung cancers. It also has a small-molecule candidate. It has no marketed products and finances itself through equity, having listed on NYSE American (KAPA) in 2024. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Kazia Therapeutics is an Australian oncology drug developer, based in Sydney, whose lead drug paxalisib is a brain-penetrant PI3K/mTOR inhibitor studied in glioblastoma and breast cancer, alongside earlier assets such as EVT801. It earned licence income from a deal on Cantrixil and related assets. Listed on Nasdaq (KZIA) and the ASX (KZA), it has no approved products and relies on equity financing. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

Ionetix is a US medical isotope company, based in Lansing, Michigan, that produces ammonia N-13 for cardiac PET imaging using compact cyclotron systems and a network of production sites close to hospitals. It sells doses and related services to cardiology imaging centres, and also has a business in cyclotron equipment. It is privately held and venture backed, and the listed flag in the data may be an error. B2B healthcare supplier with no consumer brand profile.

Longeveron is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company, based in Miami, developing Lomecel-B, a cell therapy made from donor-derived medicinal signalling cells, for hypoplastic left heart syndrome in infants, Alzheimer's disease and ageing-related frailty. It also earns small amounts from contract manufacturing and clinical trial activity. Listed on Nasdaq (LGVN) and has no approved products. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

MAIA Biotechnology is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, based in Chicago, developing THIO (6-thio-dG), a telomere-targeting cancer drug that triggers cell death in cancer cells with active telomerase, studied with cemiplimab in non-small cell lung cancer. It has no product revenue and is funded by equity, with listing on NYSE American (MAIA) since 2022. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

Medicenna Therapeutics is a Canadian clinical-stage immunotherapy company, based in Toronto, developing MDNA11, an engineered IL-2 super-agonist, and IL-4 and IL-13 empowered superkines, for solid tumours. Its lead trial is combining MDNA11 with checkpoint inhibitors in advanced cancers. It has no marketed product and is financed by equity raises and grants. Listed on the TSX and Nasdaq (MDNA). B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

NanoViricides is a US clinical-stage nanomedicine company, based in West Haven, Connecticut, developing nanoviricide drugs that mimic cell receptors to trap and neutralise viruses, with lead candidates for shingles (NV-387 and NV-CoV-2) and other viral infections. It owns a manufacturing facility in Shelton, Connecticut. It has no commercial products and depends on equity funding. Listed on NYSE American (NNVC). B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

NewcelX is a Swiss biotechnology company based in Stans, Nidwalden, tagged by Crunchbase under biopharma and biotechnology and flagged as listed. No description is given, but the name suggests cell-based therapies. Its pipeline, partners, ownership and listing details cannot be confirmed from the available data. Small Swiss biotech firms usually have no consumer brand profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Onconetix is a US specialty biopharmaceutical company, based in Cincinnati, focused on men's health and oncology. It markets Proclarix, a blood test to improve prostate cancer risk assessment in the EU, and ENTADFI, a combination drug for benign prostatic hyperplasia acquired from Veru. The company was formerly Blue Water Biotech, which acquired Proteomedix in 2023, and it lists on Nasdaq (ONCO). It has small revenue and a history of heavy losses. B2B pharma with little consumer awareness.

OSR Holdings is a US-listed holding company, based in Bellevue, Washington, with Korean-linked operations in biopharma and healthcare, built around drug and cell therapy programmes and small commercial assets. It listed on Nasdaq (OSRH) in 2025 after a merger with Bellevue Life Sciences Acquisition Corp. Revenue is small. It is a B2B pharma holding company with little consumer awareness and a limited marketing budget.

Oxford BioDynamics is a UK precision medicine company, based in Oxford, whose EpiSwitch technology maps three-dimensional chromosome conformations to create blood-based biomarkers, used to predict response to cancer immunotherapy, detect prostate cancer and stratify patients in clinical trials. Customers are pharma companies and clinical laboratories, paying for services and test kits. Listed on London's AIM market (OBD). Small B2B diagnostics business with no consumer brand and limited sponsorship budget.

PDS Biotechnology is a US clinical-stage immunotherapy company, based in Princeton, New Jersey, developing cancer treatments built on its Versamune T cell-activating platform, notably PDS0101 for HPV16-positive head and neck cancer, tested in combination with the checkpoint inhibitor pembrolizumab. It partners with Merck and the National Cancer Institute for research, has no approved product, and funds operations through equity and grants. Listed on Nasdaq (PDSB). B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

Revelation Biosciences is a US clinical-stage life sciences company, based in San Diego, developing Gemini, a trained-immunity therapeutic aimed at preventing and treating acute kidney injury and inflammation after surgery, plus a diagnostic test for chronic kidney disease. It has no commercial products and is financed by equity raises. Listed on Nasdaq (REVB) following a 2022 SPAC merger. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

Satellos Bioscience, formerly ICo Therapeutics, is a Canadian biotechnology company, based in Toronto, developing SAT-3247, an oral drug that restores muscle stem cell polarity to improve repair in Duchenne muscular dystrophy and related muscle disease. It is advancing the drug through early clinical trials. The company has no commercial products and funds research via equity raises. Listed on the TSX (MSCL). B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Serina Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company, based in Huntsville, Alabama, with a POZ polymer platform that improves the delivery of small-molecule and other drugs. Its lead programme SER-252 is a continuous-delivery apomorphine for Parkinson's disease, and the company also works with pharmaceutical partners on drug-delivery licensing. It listed on NYSE American (SER) in 2024 via a merger with AgeX Therapeutics. Revenue is limited. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Sonoma Pharmaceuticals is a US specialty pharmaceutical and medical device company that makes stabilised hypochlorous acid products under the Microcyn brand, for wound care, skin care and eye care, and sells them to hospitals, clinics, distributors and consumers. It manufactures in Mexico and sells mainly in the US, Mexico, Europe and Asia, using partners. Listed on Nasdaq (SNOA), it was formerly Oculus Innovative Sciences and moved its base to Colorado. Product brands such as Regenacyn are known to clinicians more than the public.

Suven Life Sciences is an Indian drug discovery company, based in Hyderabad, that has focused on central nervous system disorders, with its lead candidate masupirdine, a 5-HT6 receptor antagonist, studied for agitation in Alzheimer's disease. It is related to the Suven group, whose contract manufacturing arm Suven Pharmaceuticals was acquired by the private equity firm Advent International. Listed on Indian exchanges, it has little revenue and depends on research funding. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

Teknova is a US life sciences supplier, based in Hollister, California, that makes custom and catalogue molecular biology reagents, such as culture media, buffers, agar plates and chemical solutions, for pharmaceutical, biotech and diagnostic customers, including those making vaccines, cell and gene therapies and COVID tests. Revenue comes from product sales. Listed on Nasdaq (TKNO) after a 2021 IPO. B2B supplier with moderate recognition among lab scientists and no consumer brand profile.

Tevogen Bio is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company, based in Warren, New Jersey, developing off-the-shelf, genetically unmodified T cell therapies designed to target viral infections and cancers, such as its long COVID and Epstein-Barr virus programmes. It uses a precision T cell platform called ExacTcell. It listed on Nasdaq (TVGN) through a 2024 merger with Semper Paratus Acquisition. It has no commercial products and relies on equity funding. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

Transcode Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage RNA oncology company, based in Boston, developing RNA therapeutics for cancer using a lipid-nanoparticle delivery platform. Its lead drug TTX-MC138 inhibits microRNA-10b and is being tested in patients with metastatic solid tumours. Founded by researchers from Massachusetts General Hospital, it is listed on Nasdaq (RNAZ), has no revenue, and funds itself through equity. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

TuHURA Biosciences is a US clinical-stage immuno-oncology company, based in Tampa, Florida, developing IFx-2.0, an innate immune agonist given as an injection into tumours, with a Phase 3 programme in Merkel cell carcinoma in combination with checkpoint inhibitors, plus antibody-drug conjugates aimed at myeloid-derived suppressor cells. It listed on Nasdaq (HURA) in 2024 through a merger with Kintara Therapeutics. No product revenue. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Turn Therapeutics is a US biotechnology company in Westlake Village, California, tagged by Crunchbase under biotechnology and health care and flagged as listed. No description is given. It seems to be a small drug developer, possibly with topical products, but its pipeline, ownership, listing venue and scale cannot be confirmed from the available data. Small biotech firms like this normally have no consumer brand profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

VERAXA Biotech is a German biotechnology company, based in Heidelberg, tagged by Crunchbase under biotechnology and financial services and flagged as listed. No description is available. It appears to be a development-stage drug company, possibly connected with a SPAC listing, but the products, pipeline, ownership and listing venue cannot be confirmed from the available data. Early-stage biotech firms have no consumer brand profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Vyome Therapeutics is a US biotechnology company, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, with research operations in India, developing treatments for immuno-inflammatory diseases and anti-infectives, including a topical antibiotic for acne. It became a listed company through a 2025 merger with ReShape Lifesciences, trading as Vyome Holdings on Nasdaq. Revenue is minimal and it is funded by equity. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Advicenne is a French specialty pharmaceutical company, based in Paris, that developed Sibnayal, a potassium-citrate and bicarbonate granule treatment for distal renal tubular acidosis, a rare kidney disorder, and other formulations for kidney stones and metabolic disorders. It sold the drug in Europe through its own team and partners. Listed on Euronext Growth Paris, it ran into financial difficulties and sought restructuring. Customers are nephrologists and hospitals. B2B pharma with no consumer profile and little marketing capacity.

AquaBounty Technologies is a US aquaculture company that developed AquAdvantage salmon, a genetically engineered Atlantic salmon that grows faster, farmed in land-based recirculating systems and approved by US and Canadian regulators. Based in Maynard, Massachusetts, it sold fish from farms in Indiana and Canada to food service and retail buyers. It ran into losses and sold or wound down its farms in 2024-2025. Listed on Nasdaq (AQB). B2B seafood producer with minimal consumer awareness, and a controversial profile.

Atrium Therapeutics is a San Diego, California, biopharmaceutical company, tagged by Crunchbase under biopharma and biotechnology and flagged as listed on a stock exchange. No description is provided, and the pipeline, ownership, listing venue and scale cannot be confirmed from the available data. The name may be a recent rename of an existing listed company, so identification needs checking. Drug developers of this kind have no consumer brand profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

BioStem Technologies is a US regenerative medicine company, based in Pompano Beach, Florida, that processes and sells human placental tissue allografts for wound care, including amniotic and umbilical tissue products. It supplies physicians, wound care centres and distributors, and demand is influenced by Medicare coverage rules for skin substitutes. It trades on the over-the-counter market (BSEM). B2B medical products company with no consumer brand profile.

Bone Biologics is a US medical device company, based in Burlington, Massachusetts, developing NELL-1 combined with a demineralised bone matrix as a bone graft substitute for spinal fusion surgery. It has run trials in degenerative disc disease and seeks regulatory approval, and has no product revenue. Listed on Nasdaq (BBLG), it relies on equity financing. Customers would be spine surgeons and hospitals. B2B medtech with no consumer brand profile.

CNS Pharmaceutical is a US clinical-stage pharmaceutical company, based in Houston, developing Berubicin, a doxorubicin analogue designed to cross the blood-brain barrier, for glioblastoma and other brain tumours. The drug has been tested in a Phase 2 trial in adults with recurrent glioblastoma, and the company has explored further development options. Listed on Nasdaq (CNSP), it has no product revenue and funds itself through equity. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Curatis is a Swiss biopharmaceutical company based in Liestal, Basel-Landschaft, tagged by Crunchbase under biopharma and biotechnology and flagged as listed. No description is provided, and the pipeline, partners, ownership, listing venue and scale cannot be confirmed. Small Swiss life science firms of this sort sell to pharmaceutical customers and have no consumer brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Dermata Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage dermatology company, based in San Diego, developing topical treatments for skin conditions such as acne, moderate-to-severe acne vulgaris, and rosacea. Its lead product XYNGARI (DMT310) uses spongilla-derived particles, and the company aims to launch it through dermatologists. It has no approved product, and is listed on Nasdaq (DRMA). Small B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

Dimerix is an Australian clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, based in Melbourne, developing DMX-200, an oral drug aimed at chronic kidney disease, in particular focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), in a late-stage global trial. It has also used a receptor-heteromer discovery platform to find new drug targets. It has commercial licensing arrangements with partners for different regions. Listed on the Australian Securities Exchange (DXB). No commercial products yet. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

Biostage, formerly Harvard Apparatus Regenerative Technology, is a US bioengineering company, based in Holliston, Massachusetts, developing bioengineered organ implants using its Cellframe technology, such as a tissue-engineered oesophagus for children with birth defects and cancer patients. The product is in preclinical or early development, and the company has no revenue. It trades on the over-the-counter market (BSTG) and has historically relied on small financings. B2B medtech with no consumer brand profile.

Hoth Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, based in New York, developing small-molecule and biologic candidates for dermatology and neurology, including HT-001 for rash caused by cancer therapy (EGFR inhibitors), and programmes for atopic dermatitis and Alzheimer's disease. It works through research collaborations with universities and has no approved products. Listed on Nasdaq (HOTH). B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Inotiv is a US contract research and research-models company, based in West Lafayette, Indiana, providing drug discovery and development services and supplying purpose-bred laboratory animals through its Envigo-branded research model business, which it acquired in 2021. Customers are pharmaceutical, biotech, academic and government labs. Revenue is several hundred million dollars. Listed on Nasdaq (NOTV). It has faced regulatory scrutiny and bad publicity over animal welfare, particularly relating to a Virginia facility. B2B business with a sensitive public image that makes sponsorship unlikely.

iSpecimen is a US healthcare technology company, based in Lexington, Massachusetts, that operates an online marketplace connecting researchers with human biospecimens, such as blood, tissue and fluids, from hospitals and biobanks for drug and diagnostic development. Customers are pharma, biotech and academic researchers, and it earns a fee on each transaction. Listed on Nasdaq (ISPC) following a 2021 IPO. Small B2B life sciences platform with no consumer brand profile.

Lakewood-Amedex is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing Bisphosphocin, a new class of anti-infective compounds that kills bacteria and fungi, for wound infections, diabetic foot ulcers and other resistant infections. It is based in Pennsylvania, near the Penn State campus, and was founded to commercialise technology licensed from a university and its inventors. It has no approved products. Listed through the over-the-counter market. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

Lixte Biotechnology is a US clinical-stage pharmaceutical company, based in East Setauket, New York, developing LB-100, a small-molecule inhibitor of protein phosphatase 2A that is intended to make cancer cells more sensitive to chemotherapy and immunotherapy, tested in ovarian clear cell carcinoma, sarcoma and other tumours. It has no commercial products. Listed on Nasdaq (LIXT) and funded by equity. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Medicus Pharma is a Canadian-US clinical-stage biotechnology company, based in Toronto, developing SkinJect, a doxorubicin-containing dissolvable microneedle patch for the non-surgical treatment of basal cell carcinoma, the most common type of skin cancer, in a Phase 2 trial. It has also pursued other drug-delivery assets. Listed on Nasdaq (MDCX) and the TSX Venture Exchange. No product revenue. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Oncodesign Precision Medicine is a French biotechnology and contract research company, based in Dijon, providing preclinical and translational cancer research services to pharmaceutical firms, while also developing its own drug candidates, including programmes in kinase inhibitors and radiopharmaceuticals. Revenue comes from service contracts and research collaborations with larger drug companies. It is listed on Euronext Paris (ALOPM) and is a small company with a few hundred employees. B2B services firm with no consumer brand profile.

Pentixapharm is a German radiopharmaceutical company, based in Wurzburg, developing diagnostic and therapeutic agents that target the CXCR4 receptor found on certain cancer and cardiovascular disease cells, with a lead imaging agent used for PET scans in conditions such as lymphoma and primary aldosteronism, and therapeutic versions in development. It listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in 2024. No commercial revenue yet. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

PharmaCorp Rx is a Canadian pharmacy business based in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, tagged by Crunchbase under retail and flagged as listed. The data gives no description, but the name and tag point to retail pharmacy operations in Saskatchewan. The number of pharmacies, ownership, listing venue and scale cannot be confirmed from the available information. Likely a small regional pharmacy brand with local awareness only. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

RenovoRx is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, based in Mountain View, California, developing RenovoGem, a product combining its RenovoCath catheter with gemcitabine to deliver chemotherapy directly into the arteries feeding pancreatic tumours, in the Phase 3 TIGeR-PaC trial for locally advanced pancreatic cancer. It has no marketed product and funds operations through equity. Listed on Nasdaq (RNXT). B2B drug and device developer with no consumer profile.

Tenon Medical is a US medical device company, based in California, selling the Catamaran SI Joint Fusion System, a minimally invasive implant for treating pain in the sacroiliac joint, to spine and orthopaedic surgeons in the US. Revenue is small and comes from device sales to hospitals and surgery centres. Listed on Nasdaq (TNON) since 2022. B2B medtech with no consumer brand profile.

ZYUS Life Sciences is a Canadian biopharmaceutical company, based in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, developing cannabinoid-based drug candidates for pain, neurological and inflammatory conditions, plus some nutraceutical and veterinary products. It grew out of a cannabis-focused business and has research ties to Saskatchewan institutions. It is listed on the TSX Venture Exchange. Revenue is small. B2B and development-stage with limited consumer awareness and a modest marketing budget.

Aelis Farma is a French clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, based near Bordeaux, developing a new class of drugs called CB1 signal-specific inhibitors that block the harmful effects of cannabinoid receptor over-activation without affecting normal function. Its lead candidate AEF0117 is being tested for cannabis use disorder, and the company has licensed rights to the drug to Indivior. It also works on cognitive and neurological disorders. Listed on Euronext Paris (AELIS), it has no marketed product and is funded by partner payments and equity. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

AIM ImmunoTech is a US immuno-pharmaceutical company, based in Ocala, Florida, developing Ampligen (rintatolimod), a double-stranded RNA immune modulator, being tested for pancreatic cancer and other solid tumours, with additional interest in viral diseases such as COVID-19 and chronic fatigue syndrome. The company also markets Alferon N (interferon alfa-n3) for genital warts. Listed on NYSE American (AIM), it has minimal revenue and has been through shareholder disputes. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Artelo Biosciences is a US clinical-stage pharmaceutical company, based in La Jolla, California, developing lipid-signalling drugs that modulate the endocannabinoid system. Its lead candidate ART27.13, a cannabinoid receptor agonist that acts mostly outside the brain, is being tested to increase appetite and weight in cancer anorexia-cachexia, and it has other programmes in anxiety and cancer. Listed on Nasdaq (ARTL), it has no commercial product. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Avalon GloboCare is a US-listed healthcare company, based in Freehold, New Jersey, with operations in cell therapy, clinical laboratory services and real estate, historically with links to China. It runs a clinical laboratory services business and pursues cell-based immunotherapy and diagnostic programmes, including collaborations on CAR-T technology, and owns a property in New Jersey. Listed on Nasdaq (AVCO), revenue is small. B2B healthcare company with no consumer brand profile.

Carvolix is a French biotechnology company based in Paris, tagged by Crunchbase under biotechnology and health care and flagged as listed. No description is provided. The company's pipeline, partners, ownership, listing venue and scale cannot be confirmed from the available data. Small French life science companies of this kind have no consumer brand profile and are not usually sports sponsors. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

China SXT Pharmaceuticals is a Chinese pharmaceutical company, based in Taizhou, Jiangsu, that makes and sells traditional Chinese medicine products, including prepared slices of Chinese herbal medicine, and related health products, to hospitals, pharmacies and distributors in China. It lists American depositary shares on Nasdaq (SXTC) and has been loss-making with small revenue. B2B and distributor-led, with minimal brand awareness beyond China's herbal medicine trade.

Co-Diagnostics is a US molecular diagnostics company, based in Salt Lake City, that develops and manufactures PCR-based tests using its patented CoPrimer technology, including the Logix Smart COVID-19 test, and tests for tuberculosis and other infectious diseases, and sells a handheld Co-Dx PCR platform for point-of-care use. It sells to laboratories, hospitals and public health programmes in the US, India and other markets. Revenue surged during the pandemic then declined sharply. Listed on Nasdaq (CODX). B2B diagnostics firm with no consumer profile.

Intelligent Bio Solutions is a medical technology company, with roots in Australia and offices in New York and the UK, that sells the Intelligent Fingerprinting Drug Screening System, a non-invasive test that detects drug use from a fingerprint sweat sample in minutes, used by employers, drug treatment services and in workplaces and the criminal justice sector. Its test cartridges are sold on a consumable basis. Formerly GBS Inc, it is listed on Nasdaq (INBS) and has small revenue. B2B product with little consumer awareness.

Kane Biotech is a Canadian biotechnology company, based in Winnipeg, developing antimicrobial and anti-biofilm technologies for wound care, oral care and animal health, including pet oral-care products and the DispersinB enzyme. It sells products through distributors and licence partners, and revenue is small. Customers are veterinarians, pet owners, healthcare providers and industrial partners. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (KNE). B2B biotech with modest consumer exposure through pet oral-care products.

Lexaria Bioscience is a Canadian and US drug delivery technology company, based in Kelowna, British Columbia, with a patented DehydraTECH technology that improves how fat-soluble active ingredients such as cannabinoids, nicotine and GLP-1 drugs are absorbed in the body. It earns small revenue from licensing and research, and runs early clinical studies of GLP-1 and hypertension drug formulations. Listed on Nasdaq (LEXX). B2B technology licensor with no consumer brand profile.

Liminatus Pharma is a US company with a Wilmington, Delaware, address, tagged by Crunchbase under biopharma, biotechnology and advice, and flagged as listed. No description is provided. It appears to be an early-stage drug company, possibly linked to a SPAC-style listing, but the pipeline, ownership, listing venue and scale cannot be confirmed from the available data. Such firms usually have no consumer brand profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Microba Life Sciences is an Australian microbiome company, based in Brisbane, that offers gut microbiome tests and analysis, including the MetaXplore sequencing platform and the Microba Insight test, plus development of live biotherapeutic drugs for conditions such as ulcerative colitis and for supporting cancer immunotherapy. Customers are clinicians, researchers, pharma partners and consumers. It was founded by researchers from the University of Queensland and is listed on the ASX (MAP). Small company with some consumer awareness through gut-health testing.

OKYO Pharma is a UK-incorporated clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, with an office in London, developing treatments for inflammatory eye diseases and pain, led by OK-101, a lipidated chemerin-peptide candidate for neuropathic corneal pain and dry eye disease. It has no marketed product, relies on equity raises and has a very small team. Listed on Nasdaq (OKYO) and previously on the London AIM market. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile and little marketing capacity.

Ondine Biomedical is a Canadian life sciences company, based in Vancouver, that develops photodisinfection technology for killing bacteria, viruses and fungi using light-activated agents, notably the Steriwave nasal photodisinfection system used to reduce surgical site infections by decolonising patients' noses before surgery. It sells to hospitals, mainly in Canada and the UK, and holds regulatory approvals in some markets. Listed on the London AIM market. B2B medical company with no consumer brand profile.

Origin Agritech is a Chinese agricultural biotechnology company, based in Beijing, that breeds, produces and sells hybrid corn seed and other crop seeds, with a focus on genetically modified traits for the Chinese market. It sells to farmers through distributors and has had multi-year operating losses. Listed on Nasdaq (SEED) as a foreign issuer. B2B agricultural supplier with brand recognition among Chinese farmers, but no consumer or global sports-marketing profile.

SenesTech is a US biotechnology company, based in Phoenix, Arizona, that sells ContraPest, a liquid bait that reduces fertility in rats, offered to pest control operators, municipalities and agricultural users as a non-lethal way of reducing rodent populations. Revenue is small, from product sales and some government and commercial contracts, and the company has recorded steady losses. Listed on Nasdaq (SNES). B2B pest-control brand with little consumer recognition.

Sernova is a Canadian clinical-stage biotechnology company, based in London, Ontario, developing the Cell Pouch System, an implantable device that holds therapeutic cells, aimed at treating insulin-dependent diabetes by implanting islet cells, and later other hormone-deficient diseases. It works with partners on stem-cell-derived islet cells. The company has no commercial product and raises equity. Listed on the TSX and the OTC markets (SVA). B2B drug and device developer with no consumer brand profile.

Shuttle Pharmaceuticals is a US clinical-stage specialty pharmaceutical company, based in Rockville, Maryland, developing radiation sensitisers for cancer, led by Ropidoxuridine (IPdR), an oral prodrug of a radiosensitiser in trials for glioblastoma, a deadly brain tumour. The company also works on cancer imaging technology. It has no commercial product, and listed on Nasdaq (SHPH) in 2022. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Sunshine Biopharma is a pharmaceutical company, headquartered in Florida per Crunchbase with its main operations in Montreal, Quebec, selling generic prescription and oncology drugs, nutritional supplements and over-the-counter products through its Nora Pharma subsidiary, which has a large generic portfolio. It also develops anticancer compounds in early research. Listed on Nasdaq (SBFM). Revenue comes from generic drug sales to pharmacies and hospitals in Canada. B2B pharma with limited consumer awareness.

Theralase Technologies is a Canadian medical technology company, based in Toronto, developing light-activated and radiation-activated anti-cancer drugs, known as photo dynamic compounds, with a lead candidate for non-muscle invasive bladder cancer, tested with laser light. It also sells therapeutic laser systems for pain relief to chiropractors and clinics, which gives it modest revenue. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (TLT). B2B medtech with no major consumer brand profile.

Vitrafy Life Sciences is an Australian biotechnology company, based in Ballarat, Victoria, that has developed a cryopreservation platform for freezing and storing biological products such as blood, cells and tissues so that they last longer and can be transported more easily, with a focus on blood products. Its customers would be blood banks, hospitals and cell therapy producers. It has no commercial revenue yet and is funded by equity. B2B life science technology firm with no consumer profile.

RefleXion Medical is a US radiation oncology company, based in Hayward, California, that developed the X1, a radiotherapy system combining a linear accelerator with PET imaging so that the tumour itself guides the radiation beam, known as biology-guided radiotherapy (SCINTIX). It aims to treat tumours that move and metastatic disease, and sells to cancer centres and hospitals. It is venture-backed and received FDA clearances. B2B medical device company with no consumer brand profile.

about: Danimer Scientific was a US bioplastics company, based in Bainbridge, Georgia, that produced Nodax PHA, a biodegradable plastic made by fermentation from vegetable oils, for use in items such as straws, coffee pods, packaging and cutlery, and sold to consumer brand and packaging customers. It listed via a SPAC merger in 2020 on the NYSE (DNMR), and struggled with losses and debt. It filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2025. B2B materials supplier with no consumer brand, though it had links to major beverage and food brands.

VWR is a global supplier of laboratory products, chemicals, consumables, equipment and services to science, health and industry, selling through catalogues, e-commerce and a field sales force to pharmaceutical, biotech, hospital, university and industrial laboratories worldwide. Based in Radnor, Pennsylvania, it was owned by private equity firm Madison Dearborn and listed before Avantor acquired it in 2017 for about 6.4 billion dollars, and it now operates as part of Avantor under the VWR brand. B2B brand with strong recognition among laboratory scientists but not the general public.

Vitrolife is a Swedish medical technology and life sciences company, based in Gothenburg, that supplies products used in fertility treatment (IVF), such as culture media, instruments, time-lapse embryo imaging systems and genetic testing services, together with transplantation products. Customers are fertility clinics and hospitals in more than a hundred countries. Revenue is in the billions of Swedish kronor. It is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (VITR). B2B brand known to embryologists and fertility clinics, but not to the public.

about: GW Pharmaceuticals was a Cambridge, UK biopharmaceutical company that developed cannabinoid medicines, notably Epidiolex, an FDA-approved purified cannabidiol oral solution for severe childhood epilepsy such as Dravet and Lennox-Gastaut syndromes, and Sativex, a cannabis-based spray for multiple sclerosis spasticity. Listed on Nasdaq (GWPH), it was acquired by Jazz Pharmaceuticals in 2021 for about 7.2 billion dollars. Customers were neurologists and patients through pharmacies. Known in pharma, with moderate public awareness.

IMS Health was a Danbury, Connecticut healthcare information company that tracked pharmaceutical prescriptions and sales, supplying data and analytics to drugmakers, payers and governments. Founded in 1954, it was taken private by TPG, CPPIB and Leonard Green in 2010, listed again in 2014, and merged with Quintiles in 2016 to form Quintiles IMS, now IQVIA, a Fortune 500 company. B2B data brand, well known in pharma but not to consumers.

Portola Pharmaceuticals was a South San Francisco biopharmaceutical company that developed Andexxa, a reversal agent for factor Xa inhibitor blood thinners, and Bevyxxa, an oral anticoagulant. Listed on Nasdaq (PTLA), it was acquired by Alexion Pharmaceuticals in 2020 for roughly 1.4 billion dollars. Customers were hospitals and clinicians. B2B pharma brand with no consumer visibility. Andexxa is sold to hospitals for life-threatening bleeding in patients taking Eliquis or Xarelto, at a price of tens of thousands of dollars per course.

TESARO was a Waltham, Massachusetts oncology biotech, listed on Nasdaq (TSRO), that developed and sold Zejula (niraparib), a PARP inhibitor for ovarian cancer, and Varubi, an anti-nausea drug. It was acquired by GlaxoSmithKline in January 2019 for about 5.1 billion dollars. Customers were oncologists and hospitals. Pharma-sector brand with no consumer profile. Zejula was a leading PARP inhibitor, approved in 2017 for maintenance treatment of ovarian cancer, and the GSK deal was among the larger oncology acquisitions of its year.

Alder Biopharmaceuticals was a Bothell, Washington biotech, listed on Nasdaq (ALDR), developing antibody drugs, mainly eptinezumab (Vyepti), an intravenous preventive treatment for migraine. It was acquired by Lundbeck in 2019 for about 2 billion dollars. Customers were neurologists and infusion centres. Pharma-only brand with no consumer visibility, absorbed into Lundbeck. Vyepti was approved by the FDA in February 2020 as the first intravenous CGRP preventive for migraine and is now sold by Lundbeck.

Dermira was a Menlo Park, California dermatology biopharmaceutical company, listed on Nasdaq (DERM), that developed and marketed Qbrexza, a topical for excessive underarm sweating, and Cimzia for psoriasis, with lebrikizumab rights for atopic dermatitis licensed to Almirall. Eli Lilly acquired it in 2020 for about 1.1 billion dollars. Customers were dermatologists. Specialist pharma brand with limited public awareness. It marketed Qbrexza as a once-daily cloth wipe, and Lilly gained US rights to lebrikizumab, later developed as Ebglyss, through the deal.

Intercept Pharmaceuticals was a Morristown, New Jersey biotech, listed on Nasdaq (ICPT), that developed Ocaliva (obeticholic acid) for primary biliary cholangitis, a rare liver disease, and was developing treatments for NASH. It was acquired by Italy's Alfasigma in 2023 for about 800 million dollars. Customers were hepatologists and patients via specialty pharmacies. Pharma-focused brand with no consumer profile. Ocaliva was approved in 2016 and generated several hundred million dollars in annual sales before the FDA rejected the NASH filing.

Melinta Therapeutics was a Parsippany, New Jersey antibiotics company, listed on Nasdaq (MLNT), that sold Baxdela, Vabomere, Orbactiv and Minocin IV for serious bacterial infections to hospitals. Heavy debt led to Chapter 11 in 2019, and its assets were bought by Deerfield Management, which continued the business privately. B2B hospital pharma brand with no consumer profile. Its antibiotics were largely acquired from other companies, and the bankruptcy followed heavy debt and slow product uptake.

Wellcome Trust is a London-based global charitable foundation, with an endowment of around 40 billion pounds, funding health research, including biomedical science, public health, climate and health and mental health. It supports researchers through grants, runs the Wellcome Collection museum and library, and co-funded the Human Genome Project and the Wellcome Sanger Institute. Funded by endowment returns rather than sales. Well known in science and policy circles, with moderate public recognition, and it is a charity rather than a commercial sponsor.
